objectives.title: Find details in a short text

lessons.explanation: Present ir is voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. Put a before a destination; a + el contracts to al. Ir means going somewhere, not being there.
commonMistakes: Use voy, not vo or iro. A la stays two words; a el becomes al.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Question words carry accents: qué, quién, cuándo, dónde, adónde, cómo, por qué. Adónde asks toward where; dónde asks location. A yes/no question can use statement order with question intonation.
commonMistakes: Por qué asks why; porque introduces an answer. Do not omit the accents in direct questions.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Read the question first. Find the sentence that gives that detail, and check who, when or where it describes.
examples: ¿Cuándo? Look for the time or day.
commonMistakes: A familiar word alone may not answer the question. Check the whole message.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra strategy lesson; author review, not an independent educator audit.

lessons.explanation: Read the question, then listen for its detail. Replay as needed. Reading the transcript makes it supported practice.
examples: Listen for names, numbers and places.

stimuli.SpanishText: Hoy es sábado. Ana va a la biblioteca a las diez. Yo voy al parque con Luis a las once. Nosotros vamos al café después. ¿Adónde van Elena y Pablo? Ellos van al museo. El museo está cerca del parque. ¿Cuándo vamos todos a casa? Vamos a casa a las cinco. Mi madre pregunta «¿Por qué vas al parque?». Voy porque me gusta caminar con mis amigos.
stimuli.provenance: Original fictional passage, authored for Palabra. Not a textbook reading.
